name: Ahner Industrial Fabricating & Sheet Metal
old_description: With 2 - 5 ton overhead cranes and plenty of jib cranes we are equipped to fabricate and move your larger products or designs
about:
Ahner Industrial Fabricating & Sheet Metal operates a 45,000-square-foot fabrication facility in Sandusky, Ohio. The family-owned shop traces its roots to the Ahner Sheet Metal business that has been part of the Sandusky industrial landscape for decades, though a specific founding year is not publicly stated. Today the company runs cutting, forming, welding, and assembly under one roof, supported by 2- to 5-ton overhead cranes and multiple jib cranes for handling large weldments and structural assemblies.

The shop focuses on short-run and repeat production of metal components, from laser-cut and formed brackets to full industrial ductwork packages and large welded frames for equipment such as heater houses. Capabilities span laser cutting, press-brake forming, MIG/TIG welding, finishing, hardware installation, and final assembly. Work can start from a complete CAD model, a 2D drawing, a photograph, a hand sketch, or an existing sample part that needs replication.

Ahner serves a broad industrial base including automotive, electronics, air handling, material handling, lighting, food processing, industrial machinery, amusement parks, steel and foundry operations, construction, general manufacturing, injection molding, chemical, marine, containers, oil and energy, and quarry operations. Typical projects involve replacement parts for legacy equipment, pilot builds for new designs, and ongoing production releases for OEMs and maintenance departments.

The company emphasizes a single-point-of-contact approach: customers work directly with the fabrication team to define process scope, critical fits, material selection, inspection requirements, and delivery logistics before any work is committed. An online Price CAD tool supports instant quoting for production-ready sheet metal parts, while custom requests move through a structured review of manufacturability and timing.

about:
Airslamit operates from Gilbert, Arizona, as an online retailer specializing in air ride suspension systems for classic cars and trucks. The founding year and ownership structure are not disclosed in public materials; the storefront is staffed by personnel including a team member named Thomas who assists customers with product selection.

The company curates and sells complete air ride kits and individual components from multiple brands, including airmaxxx, Air Lift, Slam Specialties, and AccuAir. Its catalog covers vehicle-specific kits for platforms such as 1958–2018 Chevrolet C10, Silverado, Impala, and Cadillac models; 1964–1996 GM A-, B-, and G-body cars; Buick and Riviera models; and import mini trucks. Offerings range from air springs and management systems (including AccuAir Endo-VT packages) to compressors, valves, wiring kits, and mounting hardware. Some mounting plates are noted as made in the USA.

Customers include classic vehicle restorers, custom builders, and enthusiasts seeking bolt-on air suspension upgrades. The site organizes kits by make, model, and year, enabling buyers to select pre-engineered packages for applications such as 1963–1972 C10 trucks, 1958–1960 Cadillacs, or 1978–1988 G-body vehicles.

Airslamit emphasizes knowledgeable support and shipping speed: the homepage highlights free shipping to the lower 48 states, international checkout options, and reviews that cite fast delivery and detailed guidance from staff.

name: Aisin Manufacturing Illinois, LLC
old_description: AISIN’s vision is to be recognized as a World Class Organization.
about:
Aisin Manufacturing Illinois, LLC operates in Marion, Illinois. The company traces its roots to October 2001, when a groundbreaking ceremony marked the establishment of the first Aisin plant in the state. The facility began as an assembly operation for sunroofs, power slide door modules, and door locks. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed, but the entity is part of the global Aisin Group.

Today the company runs three plants in the Marion community: Aisin Manufacturing Illinois (AMI), Aisin Light Metals (ALM), and Aisin Electronics Illinois (AEIL). AMI handles assembly of sunroofs, power slide door modules, and door locks. ALM produces bumper reinforcements and ABS bodies. AEIL focuses on electronic components. Together the sites cover assembly, light-metal fabrication, and electronics manufacturing, though specific facility sizes, headcounts, and annual volumes are not disclosed.

The primary market is the automotive industry, supplying components such as sunroof systems, door modules, and structural reinforcements to vehicle manufacturers. No specific customer names are provided in the available information.

Aisin Illinois states its vision is to be recognized as a World Class Organization, achieved through a relentless pursuit to exceed the expectations of customers, team members, and the community.

name: Ajinomoto Foods North America
old_description: We craft our foods with the utmost care and respect, using only the finest ingredients for an everlasting flavor and memory.
about:
Ajinomoto Foods North America operates from Portland, Oregon, as the North American arm of the global Ajinomoto Group. The company traces its roots to the group's founding over a century ago with a mission to solve social issues through food, and it became the first to bring frozen potstickers and breaded mozzarella sticks to market.

The company produces a wide range of ethnic frozen appetizers—Asian, Mexican, and American styles—across multiple facilities including plants in Portland, Toluca, and Fort Worth. Its manufacturing process emphasizes hand-selected ingredients from qualified suppliers, in-house cooking and assembly, and a sensory evaluation program called Descriptive Analysis that uses trained panelists to assess appearance, texture, aroma, and flavor. Continuous improvement is driven by Kaizen practices, including equipment checklists and regular inspections.

Products reach customers through foodservice, grocery, warehouse club, and custom manufacturing channels. The company serves broad consumer markets with branded and private-label items, though specific client names are not disclosed.

Ajinomoto Foods North America differentiates itself through its "Eat Well. Live Well." philosophy, a commitment to ingredient quality verified by annual supplier audits, and safety innovations such as the iWarehouse forklift monitoring system deployed at its Fort Worth location. Environmental initiatives, including carbon-reduction projects at several sites, reflect its stated focus on sustainability.

name: Alabama Chanin
old_description: Now a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with cultural heritage and craft preservation at its core.
about:
Alabama Chanin operates from Florence, Alabama, where it began in 2000 with a documentary film titled Stitch and 200 hand-crafted T-shirts made by artisans in the Shoals region. The organization formally established as Alabama Chanin in 2006 and now functions as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit under Project Threadways, a single not-for-profit entity that also encompasses The School of Making and arts and humanities programs.

The company designs and produces textiles by hand, specializing in artisan-led clothing and made-to-order pieces crafted from organic cotton fabrics using slow, intentional methods. Its manufacturing practice includes hand-sewing, fabric painting, embroidery, and pattern making, all performed in its Florence facility known as The Factory. A new headquarters and community space, The Maker Lab broke ground in January 2026 to house studios, workshop rooms, exhibitions, a café, and retail. The organization also publishes books, kits, and patterns, and runs workshops teaching sewing, embroidery, and design exploration for over 100 participants per session.

Alabama Chanin serves direct consumers purchasing high-end garments (priced from $698 to $2,858), craft-education participants, and attendees of its Project Threadways symposiums on sustainability and textile culture. Past collaborations include a long-standing partnership with Heath Ceramics beginning in 2011, and a pandemic pivot to producing face masks in 2020. Its archive preserves two decades of oral histories, oral history interviews, and public history projects.

The enterprise was founded on the belief that making holds power—emphasizing transparent supply chains, ethical labor, cultural heritage preservation, and creative placemaking. Its mission integrates production, education, and documentation to sustain artisan craft and keep continuity between makers, materials, and place.

Its service portfolio includes industrial mechanical contracting, general contracting, plant-wide maintenance programs, field construction, and custom metal fabrication. The company does not publish facility square footage, employee count, or production volumes, but describes its team as experienced professionals dedicated to timely, quality work.

The firm markets itself to companies throughout the Southeast, without specifying particular industry sectors or customer names. Its website navigation highlights fabrication, field construction, equipment, and work in progress as primary activity areas.

about:
Scholar Craft has operated from Warrior, Alabama since 1956, when the company began producing American-made school furniture. The business remains focused on manufacturing classroom furnishings for educational institutions.

The company designs and manufactures a range of classroom furniture including student desks, tables, teacher workstations, seating, and storage solutions. Product lines such as the Structure Series and Form Series are built for daily use in demanding learning environments. Manufacturing is domestic, though the facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not disclosed.

Scholar Craft serves K–12 schools, colleges, and universities, selling through dealers and directly to educators, architects, and designers who specify furniture for new construction, renovations, or single-classroom upgrades. The company also provides planning resources — specifications, finish options, catalogs, and layout tools — to support the specification process.

Scholar Craft emphasizes four pillars: domestic production, durability for daily classroom wear, flexibility to support collaborative and active learning, and planning support for specifiers. The company traces its expertise to over six decades in the educational furniture market.

name: Alabama Wire
old_description: Our wire straightening and cutting facility accommodates a broad range of materials, grades, and sizes...
about:
Alabama Wire, LLC operates from Pelham, Alabama, where it supplies cold-drawn wire and custom wireformed products for industrial and consumer applications. The company runs a wire straightening and cutting facility that handles a broad range of materials, grades, and sizes.

The company’s core operations include straightening and cutting wire to length, re-coiling wire to customer-specified lengths and packaging, and forming and fabricating wire using CNC wireformers and cutting machines. It also offers a line of nursery products designed to stabilize, protect, and promote the growth of commercially grown landscape plants. Materials processed range from low-carbon and galvanized steel to stainless steel, aluminum, and high-carbon spring temper grades.

Alabama Wire serves industrial and consumer markets, with a dedicated nursery product line for the commercial landscape sector. Its customer base includes buyers seeking a one-stop source for wire and wireformed products, from straightened and cut wire in a wide range of diameters and lengths to coiled wire available for immediate shipment from on-site inventory. The company also leverages relationships with major wire drawers to fulfill special requirements.

The company emphasizes its quality system, which integrates multi-step order review, supplier qualification, incoming material inspection, and a computer-based identification and tagging system that provides heat and lot traceability from mill to delivery. State-of-the-art cutting machines and CNC wireformers enable close tolerances, while experienced staff perform continuous inspection to maintain consistency across orders.

name: Alaska Butcher Equipment & Supply Inc.
old_description: We ship quality equipment throughout Alaska and to the contiguous 48 states.
about:
Alaska Butcher Equipment & Supply operates from Anchorage, Alaska, where it has served hunters, anglers, and commercial processors since its founding. The business is owned by Butch, who is frequently mentioned by customers as the face of the company. While the exact founding year is not publicly stated, the store has become a fixture at sportsman's shows across the state.

The company stocks a wide range of vacuum packaging machines and supplies—including chamber vacuum packers, suction sealers, and bags from brands such as Magic Vac, Flaem, and Mini-Pack—alongside meat-processing equipment: grinders, saws, stuffers, mixers, slicers, tenderizers, and smokers. It also carries sausage-making ingredients (casings, cures, seasonings, high-temperature cheese), packaging materials, protective gear, and branded apparel. In addition to sales, the shop provides equipment servicing and short-term rentals.

Customers span home users preserving wild game and fish, as well as small-scale commercial butchers and seafood processors throughout Alaska and the lower 48 states. Testimonials reference purchases of vacuum sealers, sausage stuffers, and smokers, and note the company's presence at Alaska sportsman's shows where it offers event pricing.

The company emphasizes that it stocks only quality products, stands behind what it sells, and provides friendly service with statewide and nationwide shipping. The rental and servicing programs are positioned as a way to support customers who need temporary capacity or maintenance on their equipment.

about:
Frontier Alaska Auto Parts operates in Kodiak, Alaska, as a doing-business-as name of Alaska Carquest LLC. The company serves the automotive aftermarket from its Kodiak location, providing parts to customers across the region and through its online store.

The business stocks a catalog spanning hundreds of brands and tens of thousands of part numbers. Its inventory covers starting and charging components, suspension parts, belts, hoses, water pumps, ignition and filter products, heating and air conditioning items, wipers, lamps, fuses, brake system components, chemicals, waxes, lubricants, and exhaust, clutch, and flywheel parts. The company provides a vehicle-specific parts lookup on its website — allowing searches by year, make, model, and engine — and publishes how-to installation videos for tasks such as brake replacement, distributor service, washer pump repair, and ultra-high-capacity battery installation.

Frontier Alaska Auto Parts supplies the automotive repair and maintenance market, serving professional technicians, fleet operators, and do-it-yourself vehicle owners in the Kodiak region and beyond. The breadth of brands and categories positions it as a single-source supplier for common wear items and repair components across passenger car and light truck platforms.
